evals.prompt: Use /deep-discovery to understand this inherited MVP. Nobody has a complete architecture document. Investigate the application as it exists today and tell me what is real, partial, unused, or missing.
evals.expected_output: Claude coordinates complementary scouts rather than assigning the whole repository to one agent; attempts or observes a representative document-processing workflow instead of treating a build, test, or help screen as product proof; identifies document processing as the principal value path; traces submission through queueing, worker extraction, persistence, and retrieval; distinguishes the intended flow from the fatal cross-process storage break, partial export, and unused billing stub; follows or explicitly calls out the referenced external platform configuration; and identifies ownership clues without inventing stakeholders. It writes a durable current-state report and a navigable discovery knowledge base whose schema-valid application model combines AST-established modules, imports, routes, and calls with the separate API and worker runtime, managed dependencies, capabilities, findings, unknowns, and value-path trace. It records the repository revision, static-analysis method, source roots, exclusions, coverage limits, stable model IDs, exact source locations, and a central evidence catalog; every consequential claim links to evidence and static edges do not claim runtime activity. It creates a readable architecture atlas derived from the model with a top-level runtime view and document-processing flow, preserves editable diagram source, identifies projected model IDs, and does not publish the raw symbol graph. It produces an onboarding guide and chooses either a compact combined presentation or separate discovery and onboarding decks based on the resulting complexity. The report and assets put the main finding first, use the defined evidence statuses, place code references near supported claims, and limit open questions to prioritized current-state evidence, conflict, ownership, or boundary gaps.

evals.prompt: Run /deep-discovery on this small internal data-processing application. It has no meaningful UI and mostly consists of scheduled jobs, schemas, and exports.
evals.expected_output: Claude adapts its investigation to a non-UI system; attempts a representative scheduled-job workflow when feasible; treats the schedule and incoming usage rows as triggers; traces ingestion, normalization, aggregation, and export to the finance outcome; explains the database model and checkpoint behavior; classifies the export according to what was actually observed, tested, connected, or merely declared rather than calling it active from configuration alone; and distinguishes it from the documented but absent retry dashboard. It contracts the artifact set for the small application: a canonical report; a compact knowledge base with an index, schema-valid application model, and evidence catalog; one combined system and data-flow view or similarly compact atlas; editable diagram source; a focused onboarding guide; and one combined discovery/onboarding presentation with technical detail in an appendix. The Python AST pass records its method, coverage, retained job and data-access facts, and limits without dumping every symbol. It does not manufacture topic pages, subsystem diagrams, or user-interface terminology. The writing is direct, uses consistent terms, and omits schema or configuration detail that does not explain the outcome, a boundary, capability state, risk, or navigation point.

evals.prompt: Use /deep-discovery to map this inherited MVP before we decide whether to move it into our normal cloud tenancy. Focus only on understanding the application as it exists today.
evals.expected_output: Claude creates a clear current-state product and system model, including current runtime configuration and external boundaries, but does not recommend a destination architecture, cloud migration, redesign, implementation sequence, or remediation plan. It selects distinct user outcomes rather than treating deployment variants as separate value paths, distinguishes shared code from separate runtime instances in the knowledge base and diagrams, uses the defined evidence and capability statuses, and states facts, repository claims, static findings, inference, and unknowns at the correct level of certainty. The knowledge base is revision-scoped and connects capabilities, runtime units, source structure, value-path steps, findings, and prioritized unknowns through stable IDs and a central evidence catalog. The architecture atlas expands only where separate API and worker processes, managed dependencies, or external configuration need focused views, and each view is a traceable projection of the model. The discovery and onboarding presentations reuse the report, knowledge base, and atlas without turning current-state findings into migration recommendations. The executive summary stands alone and emphasizes the three to five findings that most affect understanding. Open questions are prioritized current-state evidence gaps, repository or documentation conflicts, ownership questions, or adjacent systems outside the boundary—not future design decisions.
